utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I understand, Mr. Saxon, there may be some matter you wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Ms. Issa has a matter to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour. There's just one matter, Your Honour. Last night we were notified by the Defence that they may be using an additional exhibit which is 1D285. This matter was -- it's actually the contract of employment that relates to Zoran Krstevski. This matter was never placed on the Rule 65 ter (G) summary that was provided by the Defence in relation to this witness. Of course, we were -- we didn't have notice of this matter prior to preparing our own notice of the exhibits we intend to use with this witness. Therefore, in the event that the Defence do intend on using this document with the witness, the Prosecution objects on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the difficulty that you have?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the difficulty, is, Your Honour, that the issue of when Zoran Krstevski became an advisor to the Ministry of Interior is an important issue in this case and because it does effect the credibility of an important aspect of Witness M-052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying that there are issues here that you need time to explore or that you need time to obtain another witness or further evidence, or what is it; or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to say, Your Honour. But if we didn't have an indication, then we wouldn't have been able to place some additional documents perhaps on our own exhibit list in order to explore the issues with this particular witness. So we're left in a position where we have not had the opportunity to prepare for this particular issue, which is quite critical to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Being the pessimist that I sometimes have to be on Friday, we're certainly not going to finish this witness today.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If that's the case, you will have the weekend. Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think it would be. It would be enough, Your Honour. It's just a question of having to -- to gather the documents and add them to our exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if the problem arises and if, as I suspect, we are not going to finish the witness today, the weekend may solve it. If the witness -- if the speed of our examination and cross-examination exceeds expectation, we'll have to look again at your problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If there's no other matter, we will have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Dorevska. You will recall that yesterday we were discussing the duties and authorisations of the minister. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the minister cannot assign duties and tasks to himself, but that they are regulated by legal acts. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be given binder number one, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would you take a look at the document that comes after tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P86, and Article 25 of that document or law. In paragraph 1 of Article 25, it is 8986 is the page new in Macedonian; and in English, it is N000-8967.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Article 1 -- or rather, paragraph 1 of Article 25 says that: "The minister provides the application form and the procedure for issuing identification cards to the authorised officials." Tell me now, Ms. Dorevska, is this an example of the authorisations given by the law to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the ways which it establishes how the minister has the authorisation for a certain task.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's take a look at Article 61, which is N000-8994 in Macedonian; and in English, it is N000-8976.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That Article states as follows: "The minister or an employee authorised by him can postpone or discontinue the annual leave of an employee." Is that a provision which confirms what you said during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is also one such provision which pertains to the same matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to indicate some of the other Articles: Articles 67; 70; 74, paragraph 2; 75 of the Law on the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which, in similar fashion deal with these issues in the way that the witness has testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, you also said that the minister can issue an order if he is authorised to do so by law or pursuant to a government decision or a parliament decision. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to take a look at Article 10, paragraph 2, of that same law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P86. And it's on page N000-8983 of the Macedonian, and N000-8964 of the English. If you look at Article 10 paragraph 2, it says: "When the public law and order are disrupted on a large-scale, the minister can order other authorised officials, under Article 24 paragraph 2 of this law, to conduct certain activities in uniforms." Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, is this one of the ways in which the law authorises the minister to issue direct orders and that was your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This Article 2 points to the fact that the minister can issue orders in this regards to the authorised officers who usually do not work in uniform, which means that by order of the minister, they're obliged in certain cases to carry out obligations in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to take a look at Article 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page N000-8987 of the Macedonian, and N000-8969 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of Article 30, it says the following -- or rather, let's see what it says in paragraph 1: "In order to prevent committing criminal offences and the discovery and apprehension of perpetrators of the critical offences, as well as finding out and securing evidence and traces of the criminal offences, the authorised officials can close the access or entrances into a certain premise or building and to prevent anybody from leaving the premises or building without permission. These measures will be in force until the completion of the official activities." Now, in paragraph 2 of this Article, it says as follows: "The minister or a person authorised by him can order the undertaking of the measures stipulated in paragraph 2 of this Article." Now, Ms. Dorevska, does this provision confirm what you yourself said, that the law or other provisions and rules can vest the minister with direct authorisation to issue direct orders?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this provision confirms this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let's move on to another area, Ms. Dorevska. Yesterday, we saw a number of acts issued by the ministry, or rather, the minister; and tell me, please, as you are the head of the sector for legal and personnel affairs, what the legal grounds are for the minister to be able to pass such enactments?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legal grounds for the minister to pass such an order is Article 55 of the Law on Organisation and Work of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which prescribes the acts under the authorisation of the ministries, including the Minister of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the law, are there any other acts that can be legal grounds for the decisions taken by the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. In the Ministry of Interior, grounds for passing certain acts of the minister are found in the collective agreement of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at the next document. It's the one found after tab 15, and we have already discussed it. But this time let's just take a look at what the legal grounds for issuing this act.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1D66, the exhibit number; and can we look at page 1D2322.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, where are the legal grounds stated authorising the minister to pass an act of some kind regardless of whether we're dealing with rules, decisions, or whatever?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning, at the top of the document, always, it is marked the legal grounds, the basis under which authorises the person who is adopting this act to adopt such an act.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in this specific instance, as we see, it is pursuant to Article 55, item 1 of the Law on the Organisation and Work of the Bodies of the State Administration, which you said was the usual basis for these decisions.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, during your testimony yesterday, you said that the minister was also linked by government decision of the president or "sobranje," or prime minister or "sobranje." Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you look at the document that comes after tab 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P74, and it is on 42-4682 of the Macedonian, and 8042-4684 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision and, as you said, provides the legal basis for a decision to be taken. As it says here, it is "based on Article 55, paragraph 1 of the Law on the Organisation and Work of the State Administration." Now tell me, please, this decision, does it have any other legal basis which the minister had to respect in order to pass a decision of this kind?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This decision for establishing a police battalion for rapid intervention, the basic Article is 55 which vests the authority to the minister to pass decisions. There are also decisions of the government of the Republic of Macedonia, and the decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. These are documents which give rise to the position of the minister to establish such a battalion, which means that these are decisions which vest the minister with the -- with this obligation, and this is why they're part of this decision as its legal grounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the next document which comes after tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit P278. Page 4690 in the Macedonian, and 4690, 4691-ET [as interpreted]. P275 is the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you look at the legal basis here, tell me if it is any different from the legal basis of the document we saw a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the same legal basis in this case as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at document -- or rather, Exhibit 1D59.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1D2329. It comes after tab 20. In the English, it is 2331.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document in view of the documents you saw previously?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision for establishing a unit for special purposes adopted by the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the next document after tab 21, Exhibit 1D60.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page is 1D2333 of the Macedonian, and 1D2336.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you recognise this document in connection with the decision and order that we saw a moment ago, as having been issued by the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. This is also a decision of the president of the Republic and one of the legal basis which are previously listed in the decision by the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, for a unit to be formed within the Ministry of Interior, what steps must be taken beforehand, before such a unit can be established, or rather, before it comes into existence as a unit within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There need to be changes or supplements, amendments to the organisational act of the ministry and for the act on systemization in order for it to become part of the organisational structure of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, we saw two decisions by the minister about the formation for the -- of the rapid intervention battalion. Now, when could this battalion have been formed and come into being as a unit of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened or this could happen at the moment when amendments are made to the act of systemization and organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at the document that comes after tab 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D61. 1D2353 is the Macedonian page number, and the English is 1D2355. Exhibit 1D61 is the document we're dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, whether it was necessary to enact these rules for amendments to the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior for the unit formed by the previous decision to be able to begin to be formed in actual terms, to come into being?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was obligatory for these rules to be passed, and this indicated in itself that the battalion for rapid intervention is established at the moment with the passing of this rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the document that comes after tab 25, which is Exhibit 1D62.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is to be found on 1D2357 of the Macedonian, and 1D2364 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These are rules on the systemization of workplaces within the Ministry of Interior. Now, in view of your legal knowledge and experience and your practical knowledge, is it possible that a unit comes into being before systemization of workplaces is determined; that is to say, the work places which that unit must fill and according to which the unit exists?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it cannot be set up. The rule on the organisation establishes the organisational form, and this must be followed with the rules on systemization of the specific work places which will indicate the structure, the number of employees, and the work positions in that concrete and specific organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in that set of rules, would you, please, take a look at page 1D2359 which begins with item 5.1,?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it is 1D2366.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, these supplements to the rules on systemization, do they provide for the structure of the unit? Does it regulate that? Is that the condition that must be met if the unit is to be established?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a condition for the unit to be established, and it points to the structure, the work places, the number of employees, the status of the workplace and work positions, and other required conditions for a specific work position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, if, for the formation of a particular unit or an organisational entity, a special procedure is required and special conditions, what then is necessary for the unit to be established in the first place? What conditions must be met?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In specific police units, by-laws are also passed. It is obligatory for such acts to be passed, which contains specific elements which pertain to that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the document that comes after tab 27.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P82 and the number is R042-4685; and in English, it is R042-4685-R042-4689-ET -- or rather, the previous page. No, we have the right page number there. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, we see here the rules on the conditions and procedure for the assignment, rights, and duties of members of the rapid intervention battalion of the Ministry of Interior which was passed in October 2001. Now, are those, indeed, the rules that must be enacted if the formation of a unit requires specific conditions to be met and you testified about that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. This is one such rules which must accompany the process of establishing a specific unit such as the one we're talking about right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, is it possible for a unit to come into being before procedure is put in place and all the conditions have been meet for each individual member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, not. It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in practice, was there ever a case in the Ministry of Interior whereby an organ was established or a unit was established before all the stipulated conditions that we've discussed have been met?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of such a case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We've just been discussing units or one particular unit. Now, is the situation the same and must the same rules be applied and procedure put in place if an organisational form within the ministry is changed or amended or supplemented in any way, or are there other rules for other organisational procedure?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure is the same for setting up any organisational form in the ministry. This is done in an identical manner with amending the Rule Book on Organisation and Systemization of Work Positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, yesterday, we looked at some diagrams relating to the organisation of work in 2001 with amendments from August, August of that year. Now, tell me whether you know -- or rather, on that diagram or on that chart, could we see that -- did see some information centre within the ministry? Was there an information centre of any kind depicted in the chart?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the framework of --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any press information centre within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. There was no such organisational unit in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Stevo Pendarovski?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what his job was and how long he worked in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I perhaps don't know the exact date; but I believe by May 2001, he was working in the ministry and then he left his position there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what his function was in the ministry, before he left the ministry, what post he occupied?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- he was the spokesperson of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the fact that you told us what was your job in 2001, before you became head of the sector for legal and personnel matters, you were working on the personnel issues before that. Tell me, do you know whether, after Stevo Pendarovski left, some other person was appointed the spokesperson of the Minister of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no person on that position after he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Dorevska, we would move to another set of questions. In your testimony thus far, you mentioned that the works of the Ministry of Interior or the tasks were carried out by the reserve police forces in addition to the regular police forces in 2001. Was that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me when is the -- when are the reserve forces called up to carry out certain tasks of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are specifically listed conditions in the Law on Internal Affairs in the case of direct danger of war when the public law and order is disrupted in a larger scale. In such case, it is possible to call in military and police reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to assist us in removing this binder from the witness' table, and giving number two of Defence exhibit to the witness. I would kindly ask that these documents are also distributed to the Chamber and to my colleagues from the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now, Ms. Dorevska, to tell me who are those individuals who are called up? Is it that before the war situation occurred that the military deployment or structure of reserve forces was decided in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are persons, as established on the Law on Defence, who have finished their military service or have in a different way regulated their military obligations and who are registered at the Ministry of Defence, more precisely, in the regional services of the Ministry of Defence, and have deployment in the case of war in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at the document after tab 35.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D154.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask about this document, tell us, are you aware what are the competences that the Minister of the Interior has in terms of reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the reserve forces, and in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs, the minister has the obligation to pass the special rules which pertains to calling in persons from the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who from within the Ministry of Interior enforces the provisions of the rule book that is enacted by the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a special organisational unit. This was the sector for Defence preparation at the time. Now it has a different title which is charged with implementing the activities regarding the police and military reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you kindly look now at the document after tab 40.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P85. R042-4706 is the Macedonian version, while the English is R042-4706-R042-4709-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, you have a general act in front of you again. The adoption of this act, as a general act, is it within the competence of the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are rules which relate to special identification documents for members of the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, tell us whether the minister has any other rights and duties with regards to the positions and the rights of the reserve forces, considering the legally prescribed competences?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minister also adopts an act which pertains to the fees for the persons who are engaged in the reserve forces because they have a legal right to such compensation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the status that the members of the police -- of the reserve forces have within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are persons, as I said, military and police conscripts which are called in a given period of time; and in accordance with the law, they have obligations and authorisations of authorised officials while they're engaged. However, they do not have a contract of employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was supposed to be my next question. Do they have an employment, full employment contract with the Ministry of Interior? You partially answered that already, but can you give me a direct answer. The members of the reserve forces, after being called up, do they have an employment status with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The member of the reserve forces do not have a full contract of employment at the Ministry of Interior. They can be employed in any other organisations or they can be unemployed persons. However, they do not include a contract for employment with the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, although we will come back to this issue later, could you just briefly tell us who are actually employees of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are persons who have a contract of employment with the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what are the regulations that provide for that employment?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the labour law, which is also a systemic law pertaining to labour relations,; the Law on Internal Affairs; and the provisions of the collective agreement of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that the witness is now given the third set of documents, considering that we will use that binder as well in the course of further examination of the witness. I kindly ask that those documents are distributed to the Chamber and my colleagues from the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, would you kindly look at the document after tab 75.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P553. N002-5377, Macedonian version, page 2; or possibly page 1 also of the English version. That is N006-323 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 6-3823.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that is the first page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to look at the second page of the document in the Macedonian version; and, tell me, is this the labour law that you described as an organic law governing this area?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the labour law of 1993 which was in force at that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look now at the document after tab 76.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P382, N006-4902; and the English is N002-6338. That is, I believe, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is this the collective agreement that you mentioned just now, which is the basis for the employment contract for the officers of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the collective agreement of the ministry adopted in 1998, which strictly regulates the provisions related to working relations for the employees at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, considering that this is the area where you worked for many years, what could be the employment status of an officer within the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The employment status can be of unlimited duration or for a limited duration. It might be also a part-time contract, but this is rarely used.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does every employee, before they become an employee of the minister, have to enter an employment contract?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signing of the employment contract is mandatory for every individual entering into employment with the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does the employment contract that the officer or the employee enters into with the ministry contain the date the contract was entered into; and if that date is contained in the document, is that the date when an individual became an employee of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. That contract is entered into for a limited or unlimited duration, as I mentioned; and, among other things, it also contains the date from which the individual starts the employment and that is also registered with the employment bureau in order to exercise other rights related to the employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, if a given person hasn't signed a contract bearing an exact date from which they become an employee, would that person be an employee of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That person is not considered an employee. That person could not be employed if they have not signed an employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If some officer does not have a contract, are they de jure or de facto, or could they be an employee of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you know Zoran Krstevski?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember when he was to start his employment with the ministry because I was working then in the personnel section. I was in charge of his employment procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he signed an employment contract with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He has signed an employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this contract indicate the date when he became the employee of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The date is a mandatory element in the employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the post that he held after he had signed that contract?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. His employment was with the cabinet of the minister. He was advisor to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that a duty denoted in his employment contract? You said that you were in charge of that procedure of that employment contract.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not understand your question well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the duty, as you said, advisor in the cabinet, was that defined in the contract that he signed with the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. His employment contract expressly states the job for which his employment contract is signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you remember, Ms. Dorevska, when did -- did this take place?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was somewhere in September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You just testified about the way in which the employment starts. In addition to this, do the elected officials base their employment on the same foundation as other officers of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, not. They do not sign an employment contract. Their employment and legal status is regulated in a different way. They are elected by the government of the Republic of Macedonia, by the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we spoke about the employment contract, I will ask you to lock now at the document after tab 77.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D89. It is in the page 1D3759, Macedonian page; while the English is 1D3761.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this document, Exhibit 1D89, in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to my previous questions, you said -- or rather, you gave us a detailed answer and said that each employee must have a contract of employment which he signs with the ministry. Now, when you look at this particular document, is it an example of an employment agreement or contract of employment that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When an employee signs a contract of employment with the minister, thereby becoming part of the staff of the ministry, in what way is he assigned to jobs or promoted to various functions within the ministry? How does that work?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any further procedure, in terms of career development of the officer, is accompanied by a specific decision for deployment or assignment to that post.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, are the conditions identical for all work posts, or is there something that stipulates the conditions to be met for each separate work post?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are general, as well as special conditions, that are identical for everyone. They are prescribed in the labour law and the Law on Internal Affairs. Of course, special conditions are prescribed in the act for systemization for each of the specific job posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the general conditions that each employee has to comply with you said were determined by what act was it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Labour law and the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask to you take a look at the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was in binder 1, and the document that comes after tab 5 -- or rather, not to have to go back to that binder, perhaps we can look at P86, Article 48 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in Article 48, we have listed the conditions which you said were general conditions that had to be complied with by each and every employee of the ministry before that person can sign a contract of employment with the ministry. Now, tell me, were all these conditions in force in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the conditions that were in force, but then the constitutional court revoked them, the first and the second item. I do not remember the exact date when they were revoked, when that entered into force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's now take a look at the document that comes after tab 70 in the second binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 65 ter 1D1217 [sic]. Did I say after tab 70? It is 1D1216, a 65 ter document, 1D1216.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we can see, under number 430, we have a decision passed by the constitutional court, passed on the 10th of April, 2002; and as we can see from paragraph 1, Article 48, paragraph 1, item 2, if the Law on Internal Affairs is rescinded. Is that the decision, Ms. Dorevska, that you were talking about, when it said it declared null and void some of the general conditions stipulated by the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the decisions, referring to item 2 in Article 48.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, from this time on, would that be the conclusion, from the 10th of April, 2002, point 2 of Article 48, paragraph 1, was no longer in force? It was no longer a general prerequisite for anybody to gain employment in the ministry. Would my conclusion be correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at the document after tab 71?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 65 ter 1D1217; and, once again, it is from the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia. May we have the document displayed in Macedonian on e-court as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, down at the bottom there, and the number is 875, we see that the constitutional court of the Republic of Macedonia, on the 23rd of May, 2001, passed a decision to abolish Article 48, paragraph 1, of the Law on Internal Affairs. Tell me, please, whether this document, this decision in fact, indicates that, by this decision of the constitutional court, Article 48, paragraph 1, item 1 was abolish on the Law on Employment [sic] that you discussed earlier on?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I got that wrong.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the decisions of the constitutional court passed previously which abolishes line 1 or item 1 of Article 48, which was previously a special prerequisite for employment with the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as of the 7th of June 2001 when this decision was published, is my understanding correct that paragraph 1, item 1, which was set out as one of the conditions for a contract with the ministry to be concluded could no longer applied? In fact, it no longer existed, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, when a constitutional court passes a decision, the decision itself indicates that that legal provision is abolished and the decisions of the constitutional court and the other courts are mandatory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When an employee meets all the general conditions and the special conditions stipulated, is there any set procedure for taking in the employee for that person becoming a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there is a procedure prescribed with the law and the secondary legislation depending on the way in which the employment is concluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, tell me, how is that put in place, what happens?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The employment could be based by a public ad or without such public ad, and depending on that an appropriate procedure is followed. If a public competition was opened, that procedure is regulated in the collective agreement. The committee is established, the committee then selects the candidates, makes a proposal, a list to the minister. And from that list, he selects the individuals who will start their employment. And if it is an employment without a public ad, then the procedure is slightly different. Then the services, the sector that I'm the head of carry out the entire procedure. And if it is established that all the requirements are met, then the person would enter employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who signs the actual contract on employment?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contract is signed by the individual who starts their employment and the minister on behalf of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can an employee sign a contract directly with the minister, as a person, and not as an organ representing the ministry? So, is it signed by the minister as an organ representing the ministry or by the person?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The employee could sign a contract only with the body, within the ministry. But on behalf of the ministry, as I said, the contract is signed by the minister. One could not sign a contract with the minister as an individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, when an employee signs such a contract of employment, tell me, please, who has the right to assign that person to a specific work post?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That right belongs to the minister to assign an officer to a different post through a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's now take a look at the law governing labour relations, and it's tab 75 in the third set of documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P553, Article 27.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I don't think I have it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the third binder. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're looking at Article 27. This is to be found on N002-5382 of the Macedonian; and in English, it is N006-3830, or page 8 of 43.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this law is a systemic law. Now, tell me, please, whether other regulations which relate to labour relations must be dove-tailed and harmonised with the basic provisions of this systemic law? ?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, they must be harmonised. Within the Ministry of Interior, the collective agreement is fully harmonised with the labour law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were talking about the minister's authorisations yesterday, you said that he -- these authorisations are vested upon him by law. Now, let's take a look at Article 27 in which it says that: "Employees engaged in work at a position for which they have been hired, in cases established in the collective agreement, employees may be reassigned to any position that corresponds to their qualification. "The decision of reassignment is brought by the employer or by his appointed employee." Now, since you said a moment ago that the act on assigning workers is passed by the minister, now, this right of his, has it got anything to do with the right of all employees, according to the systemic law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it is related to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the document after tab 76 in the collective contract or agreement of that same binder. It's Exhibit P382. Yes, 382. Take a look at Article 26 there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 6493; and in English, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This Article, as we can see, confirms or, in fact, is completely aligned with the systemic law. Now, paragraph 1 and 2, or rather, items 1 and 2 of this Article, do they say that workers can be assigned to every work post determined by the act on the systemization of work posts which corresponds to his level of skills and training? Then it goes on to state the conditions when he can be assigned to a post.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is the Article which the Ministry of Interior or the sector which I head uses to prepare decisions for employment. It states the conditions. Then this is followed, of course, by the whole procedure related to the assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at Article 31 of this collective agreement, which is on page 64921 and page 7 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Macedonian text of that Article, there's something added on in handwriting there, some changes, some corrections.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, my understanding of this is what has been added in handwriting is related to what it says next to Article 31 itself, that that's what it refers to. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that is an amendment that was made, and the number is 3/2004, so that mean notice year 2004, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 2004, there were amendments to the provisions of the collective agreement; among them, this provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if my understanding of this is correct, in 2001, this portion written by hand was not in force. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I made that clarification because, in the English text, the entire sentence has been translated, and we can't see in the English version that this second part says -- well, we can't see that it was added later. In Article -- yes. Perhaps not all that was recorded in the transcript. But as the witness said, the written, handwritten part did not exist in 2001, I'm going to read what it says there, written by hand, and it says the following: "... or by him, authorised official."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the first part of this Article, it says: "Decision for deployment is passed by the minister." Is that what was in force in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. It was in force in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this authorisation was given the minister from the systemic law that we looked at a moment ago. That authorisation was vested in him by that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask to you look briefly at a series of decisions which, on behalf of the ministry, is passed by the minister, and they are to be found in tabs ranges from 77 to 98. Once you've lacked at them, I'm going to ask you a few questions about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, it is P271, Exhibit P271, P76, P78, P61, P62, P64, P71, P72, P77, P76, P57, P58, P59, P65, P60, P63, P66, P67, P68, P69, and P70.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, just look through those documents briefly. Have you managed to look through them?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this first: What is the organisational units within the ministry which is in charge of preparing acts for the minister, regarding the assignment of a person to a particular post or promoting an employee or whatever?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the sector for legal and personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, all the acts that you've looked at, was that prepared by your department?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of these acts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And all the individuals all the persons mentioned in these acts were previously employees of the Ministry of Interior, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. These are decisions for changing of the work post.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me what these decisions decided, if I can put it that way? Do they relate to the same matters, or do they deal with different situations, different issues where the minister is using his authority under the law and passing decisions on behalf of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm able to see, these are decisions for reassignment, however, in different situations. Some decisions for reassignment are related to the changes in the work posts or promotions, if you will. In some cases, it is a confirmation of the same work post, what we talked about yesterday, by the head. The chief of the sector confirms this, confirms the changes in the act for systemization. Some of these decisions, as far as I can see, there are changes in the title of the organisational unit. The work post is identical. Some of the decisions are related to unit for special tasks. These are more specific decisions which, in themselves, differ from the others. Mainly, this is what I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that any of those types of decision, which you have enumerated and which you were able to see in these 20 or so documents that you looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat what she said there, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can any one of these decisions, regardless of what type of decision we're dealing with, can they be issued only to an employee who already has employment?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Only an employee which already is working at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would this be a opportune moment for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt, Your Honour. I wonder if I could, very briefly, raise a matter. We've heard the witness throughout her testimony refer to either a rule book or a Law on Systemization of Work Posts or Workplaces. I'm not entirely sure if this perhaps is a translation issue, but we've -- we don't have this rule book. We've tried to locate it. I've spoken to Ms. Residovic regarding this, and I believe she's indicated - correct me if I'm wrong - that she doesn't have the original form. I think there are amendments to the rule book which the Defence may have, and I just wonder perhaps could the witness be asked if she has it, so that we would be prepared to -- to use it for the purposes of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I tried to explain to my learned friend, during the break, what the situation is. The Prosecutor, through numerous witnesses and the Prosecution exhibits, gave numerous rules on amendments and supplements to acts on systemization, and the Court has it now. In the Law on Internal Affairs, numerous witnesses, including this one, said that it was within the remit of the minister to pass those acts. Now, as far as the Defence is concerned, some comprehensive act or the first act when it was passed, for the first time, it's not something that the Defence is interested in. We handed up and offered all original documents that were necessary; the act on amendments and supplements on law with regard to the "Lavovi" or Lions. So, a first act on systemization, I can ask the witness whether any such document exists in the ministry. But I don't see the relevance of this question at all, because we're talking about and discussing the acts and provisions that are of relevance to these proceedings, not to the 12.000 staff of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, I'm afraid you have lost me now. Ms. Issa is saying the witness appears to be referring to a rule book, if I can use it that way, which is not in any of the Defence or Prosecution papers. Now, are you saying that is so but it's not relevant; or are you saying there isn't such a rule book, it's a series of amendments to the Law on Internal Affairs; or are you saying something else?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not a witness. Now, I'm certain that, if the law provided for the fact that all the ministries should have the acts, we can ask the witness. But in these proceedings, neither the Prosecutor nor the Defence team offered up all acts governing systemization, just those which would be relevant to the issues we dealt with: The organisation chart, the position of the Tiger, the Lions, "Tigri," "Lavovi," so those documents. Those are ones we dealt with, and they're exhibits already. We have not provided any fresh exhibits or presented any new exhibits to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I understand what you are saying correctly, you are suggesting there is not a rule book. There are a series of, I suspect, subsidiary or delegated pieces of legislation that have dealt with individual items under the general heading of systemization of the workplace, and those that you think are relevant have been separately tendered. Is that what you're putting?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I ask the witness the question? She is, perhaps, better placed to clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As a matter of general law, I thought counsel would be on top of this, but please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to the fact that counsel can be on top of this, I would like to draw your attention to Article 75 from the law governing internal affairs, which says that the minister is duty bound to enact acts or documents regarding systemization of work and the work of the ministry and the act on the systemization of the workplaces. Now, I'm going to ask the witness something with respect to that fact, which might be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, tell me, please, in the ministry, are there acts on systemization, do they exist, and work places; and a Book of Rules governing the organisation and work of the bodies within the compensation of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. These are two basic documents, Book of Rules, on the basis of which the ministry operates. This is the rule of book on organisation, as I said yesterday, which establishes the organisational units and their authority. At the same time, the rule book on organisation is accompanied by act on systemization, which is a document which is constantly undergoing changes. If at a given period of time, these changes become numerous, then a clarified text of this document is enacted. The rule book on systemization contains all work places in the ministry. Without such a document, an employee cannot be assigned, an employee cannot be brought into service. This is a basic document for each ministry, and so it is the case with the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether that suffices, Your Honour. Is my learned friend satisfied with that answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It doesn't yet; although, Judge Thelin thinks he can see more clearly than I've managed to get. We have a basic law which is applicable, and then we have a series of ministerial acts which are amending that, or a series of individual ministerial acts made pursuant to that. Every now and again, the amendments may be collected together and a new print made. Have I got it correctly yet? Perhaps I could ask the witness. First, would you give me the name of the principle act, the principle piece of legislation or book of rules?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Book of Rules on Systemization of Work Places in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Residovic, is such a document in some form in your papers that are on e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I don't know when that first Book of Rules, that first piece of legislation, was enacted. But in the exhibits, and on our 65 ter list, every amendment to that Book of Rules which speaks of the introductions of new work or work places or new units which had not previously existed, and which are of interest for this trial, for these proceedings; therefore, I'm speaking directly of certain amendments which relate to the Tiger unit, and other amendments related to the "Lavovi," or Lions, unit, which conditions are required for someone in say a helicopter unit or dog training unit, that, too, probably is contained in this voluminous Book of Rules governing systemization. However, as far as I could see, the OTP, the Prosecutor wasn't interested in providing that document, nor did the Defence consider that that was relevant for the issues being discussed here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa, as we, at least as I, presently grasp it, the particular documents that are in the Defence papers and of which you have notice are those thought to be relevant because they deal with particular amendments to the original, those particular amendments introducing something or changing something that is relevant to this case. It is accepted that the original total document is not in the papers. Now, I do not know whether you feel that you need to see the original. I do not know whether you feel that some amendment which has been referred to by the witness is not to be found in the papers. But given the explanation, could I suggest, for the moment, that you confine yourself to the question whether any document particularly relied upon by the witness is not to be found in the papers we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That would be -- that would be fine for the moment, Your Honour. The difficulty is, though, we would like to see the original because it's difficult for us, at this stage, to say what may be relevant in the original that may have some impact or may have some revelation concerning the amendments that we see in the -- in the Defence binder. The amendments, as Your Honour may have noted, are quite short. They refer to a very specific matter or specific Article that appears to have reference to the original. Without seeing the original, it's difficult to fully comprehend the amendment. We can see what it says on its face. However, without it, it's hard to say, at this stage, what might be in the original that might assist us in understanding the matters that are being discussed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you have with you, by chance, a copy of the Rule Book of the Systemization of Work Places in the Ministry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I do not have it with me. This is a voluminous document, a document that is constantly undergoing change. There are 15.000 work places perhaps, which contain the name of the organisational unit and the workplaces in that unit and the conditions for a specific work place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa, I don't believe the matter can be taken further by the Chamber at the moment. Can I suggest that if you feel a particular amendment gives rise to an issue either with the content of that amendment or which requires reference to the original being amended, that you can discuss with Ms. Residovic whether that can be made available to you in some form. At the moment, given the nature of the document, there doesn't seem to be a great deal of reason for the matter to be pursued generally. There may be some specific issue, and that I must leave to you to identify and to take up with Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, then. Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to ask you that in resolving this issue that we just go back to one exhibit which is in our binders in these proceedings. Perhaps, it will be clearer to one and all if the witness were to explain things to us taking an example, how these amendments in systemization are done; or shall we leave that for later, not to lose time going over, covering the same ground that we've already covered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we can leave it for the moment, Ms. Residovic, and move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, we've seen a large number of decisions assigning employees to various work places and posts. Now, tell me, once the minister passes a decision on assigning an employee to a particular post, does he still retain control over that employee whom he has assigned to a specific work place?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This employee is now working in a specific organisational unit, and the head of that unit now supervises or looks into the work of that employee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, whether the law or a collective law governing labour relations and the law on the interior, internal affairs, does it stipulate the conditions that workers must meet and comply with after he signs a contract of employment, for him to be assigned to a work post later on or to remain in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After signing of the employment contract, if this person has the status of apprentice, there are conditions which he must fulfil, which means that in a given period of time, he has to pass an apprenticeship exam. Unless he or she does this, then there is an additional period of time during which he can pass this exam. If that person does not pass the exam on these two occasions, then the contract ends. There are also conditions when a person has to be sent to additional training to pass specialised exams or additional training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When an employee -- when a worker becomes an employee of the Ministry of the Interior, by signing a contract of employment, does he then have certain rights and duties?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, the employee is part of the ministry, and this person must work in accordance with the law and the rules and regulations in the ministry with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, can you tell us whether the concept of an employed worker, an employee of the Ministry of Interior, is it identical to the concept of "authorised official," which is the term that appears in Article 24 of the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Authorised official is a status of a work place; while employee of the ministry can imply other categories, categories of civil servant, who are employees of the ministry but are not authorised officials. There are persons who work on work legislation for which neither the civil service or ministry or internal affairs law does not apply. Therefore, this is one category of persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, let me ask the question in the reverse: Can you tell me whether all authorised officials are, by the same token, employees of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, not. The minister, the deputy minister, as we said, they have the status of authorised officials, are not employed in the ministry. What we spoke about today, about the reserve forces, these are persons who are not employed at the ministry but have obligations and authorisations of authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned who the reservists are, the reserve forces are, and who the employees are. Now, tell me once again: Are the reservists, in fact, employees of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Reservists are not employees of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's now take a look at the next document, which comes after tab 76, or paragraph 76, which you mentioned as a basis for gaining employment status.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P382 is the document number, N006-4902; and in the English version, it is -- well, I don't seem to have the English version. It's on e-court, on our screens. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, take a look at the first four articles of this collective agreement which is the basic document regulating the status of employees. Article 1 says as follows: "This collective agreement regulates, completes the regulation of the rights, obligations, duties, and responsibilities of the employees in the Ministry of Interior and the employer, as well as the way and scope in which these rights and duties are fulfilled, and other provisions concerning questions of interests of the employees and the employer, as well as the manner and procedure of resolving mutual relations." Article 2 stipulates the following: "The employer, in the sense of this collective agreement, is the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, hereinafter referred to as the ministry, represented by the Minister of Interior, hereinafter referred to as the minister." Then Article 3 reads: "Employees, in the sense of this collective agreement, is a person who is employed full-time for a shorter, or a full-time or part-time for indefinite or definite time, within the ministry." Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, does -- do these three Articles, in accordance to what you know and in accordance with your practice, regulate whom this collective agreement refers to, who is the employee, and who is the employer?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the provisions which clearly define the position of an employee and the position of the employer. Employees are persons who have contracts with the Ministry of the Interior. The employer is the Ministry of Interior, represented by the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 4, paragraph 1 says as follows: "The collective agreement shall be applied immediately and is compulsory for the ministry and the employees in whose name the agreement is signed." Tell me now, please, in whose name is this collective agreement signed precisely?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the name of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And with regards to the employees?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The collective agreement is signed by the representative of the trade union, which cares for the rights of the employees, and the minister on behalf of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look now, please, at Article 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is on the next page, which reads -- the page is N002-64922.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This Article reads: "The employment is to be established by signing a contract, employment contract, between the employee and the minister." Is it, again, Ms. Dorevska, the provision that you spoke about before the break, on the basis of which the employment contracts are signed between the employee and the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is that provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you stated, that the reservists were not employees, tell me, do the reservists sign a contract with the ministry about their employment or work?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The reservists do not sign any kind of contract with the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the reservists are called up to perform certain duties within the reserve force of the police, what kind of duties they have?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reservists, in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs, have the obligations and rights of authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that the e-court shows P86, that is Law on Internal Affairs, Article 46.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering one of the questions, you stated what the responsibilities and the authorisations were. Article 46, paragraph 2 reads that the time during which the members of the reserve forces carry out their duties, in terms of Article 24 of this law, they have the duties and authorisations of an authorised officer. When you were answering the question that they have the duties and the powers of an authorised officer, were you referring to this provision of the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the provision I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do they have some responsibilities? Does the law regulate their responsibilities as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the responsibility, as all other citizens, they have responsibility in the case of a criminal offence, they would certainly be held responsible for the act they committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could they be subject of a disciplinary procedure within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reservist cannot be prone to disciplinary procedure because they're not employees of the ministry; and, therefore, their employment cannot end as a result of the disciplinary procedure that is led against them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the reservists were not employees. Do they receive a salary from the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have a fee. They don't have a salary, but they are remunerated, as regulated in Article 47 on the Law on Internal Affairs, from the workplace where they carried out their activities which is -- and which are police obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned now Article 47 from the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we see this Article in the Macedonian language on the screen, I would like to ask to show the next page in English, so that the witness is able to clarify what she just stated. I apologise, Your Honours, but Article 47 has three lines only in the English language, while I see several paragraphs in Macedonian. Perhaps Article 47 starts in the previous page, because this obviously is not the translation of the Article that has three paragraphs. I would like to read it, or I would kindly ask the witness to read the Macedonian text of the Article 47, because it is obvious that the translation here does not correspond to the Macedonian original.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, would you be so kind as to read it. What does the Article 47 specify, the Article that you quoted?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For conducting the duties and tasks, the members of the reserve force have the right for allowance established according to the regulation for carrying out military service for serving in the reserve force. "Funds for remuneration as paragraph 1 of this Article are secured in the budget of the Republic. The minister will adopt by-laws regulating the manner of calling in and engagement of members of the reserve forces."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, does this provision confirm your testimony, that the reservists do not receive a salary but they have a right to certain remuneration?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. They are remunerated established by a special decision passed by the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to take the second binder and look at the document in tab 45.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1208. The page is 1D9688, and the English page is 1D0033.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, in this introductory part, where you said the legal foundation, the basis for adoption of a document is indicated, we can see that the minister invokes not only the general Article 55, but also the Article 46, paragraph 2 and 47, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Law on Internal Affairs. Are these the Articles that you read?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is this Article.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is this act?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision which establishes the remuneration for the members of the reserve forces because they carry out work tasks in the ministry related to a specific workplace. Here, it also enumerates the things which are -- they're entitled to while they're carrying out their tasks. This is salary, this is transport fees, one-time assistance in the case of death or injuries, and other fees and costs involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at the following page, 1D9689.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English page is 1D0034.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see that this act was passed by the then Minister of the Interior, Dosta Dimovska, pursuant to the competences listed the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item Roman numeral VII, we see that the decision declares null and void the previous decision dated 16th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is a previous decision which pertains to the same matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, Ms. Dorevska, when the second decision regulated the remuneration, was it the case that the employees could be -- that the reservists could be employees of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
