utterances.text: No. Even in the period of that decision, once again, we speak of remuneration, not of employees. Reservists have never been employed in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to look at the document after tab 46.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1209. The page is 1D9690 in Macedonian, and 1D0035 is the English page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision passed on the 16th of October, 2003; and as we can see from the text, that is a decision that declared the previous decision null and void, the decision of 11th of May, 2002. Is this what this document is?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, then, in the period between this decision, 11th of May, 2001 and until that moment, what was the remuneration paid to the members of the reserve forces; so throughout 2001 and 2002?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period, the reservists received the remuneration supplements which I read out previously from the 11th of May, 2001, salary for workplace for a police officers, and all the supplements to which that work post is entitled to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at the document after tab 47.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1210.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision passed on the 16th of April, 1999, by the then Minister of the Interior, Pavle Trajanov. Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, is this the decision in force until the 11th of May, when it was declared null and void by the decision that you recognised and commented upon a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decision which was valid until the next decision was passed; and, once again, it calls on the Law on Defence, a special provision which pertains to remuneration of persons who are called in to carry out the rights and obligations related to the defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, we're speaking about the reserve forces. We saw that the minister enacts the rules on the way of calling up of the members of reserve forces as a general act, then also enacts a decision on remuneration. Tell me, does the minister have any other authorisations towards the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he decides about their being called in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once they are called up - I apologise, let me just clarify this - or decides about them being called up, what did you refer it? Is it a call-up of an individual member of the reserve forces or what is it about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he passes a decision for engaging reservists not on an individual basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who then follows this, and what is the procedure through which the calling up is carried out?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then this, the Book of Rules, is followed by a specific organised unit in the ministry, and this the section on defence preparations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does the minister have any right to interfere or be involved in the carrying out of the procedure, with respect to the bodies dealing with defence preparations?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, he does not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Once a member of the reserve force is called up and deployed to a given post, who then issues or who then assigns tasks to him?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This the head and most often the commander of the police station where this person is called in to carry out the obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the members of the reserve forces are responsible as any other citizen if they commit a crime, and that they can't be held disciplinary responsible because they are not an employee of the Ministry of Interior. But if a member of the reserve force fails to perform properly the duties where they are appointed by the commander of the police station or any other senior officer under whom they are deployed, is there a way in which the ministry could act against such reservist?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an established procedure if the reserve police officer does not carry out the obligations as expected of him or due to other reasons. In that case, the head or the commander of the police station will inform the competent organisational unit. This is the section for defence preparations, which will then inform the original unit of the Ministry of Defence that this person is disengaged, and that there is no longer and no further need of his engagement within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now, Ms. Dorevska, to find in the binder 2 in the document in tab 48 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1214.1. That is 1D9768, and the English page is 1D0042.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, this is a document from the sector of internal affairs for the city of Skopje, the defence preparation department. Is this the organisational unit that you spoke about as being the unit carrying out the procedure after a decision to call up reservists is passed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is so. As within the framework of the ministry, there is a section for defence preparations, while each sector of internal affairs has a segment that works with defence preparations. In this document, we are talking about this part, that is part of the sector of the internal affairs in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 19, it should be tab "40A" [Realtime transcript read in error "48"], and not "48."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document speaks about recruitment of military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I'm not speaking well. But in line 6, it is, again, stated "48." It should be tab "40A," with the letter A.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the subject is: "Recruitment of military conscripts within the sector for internal affairs of the city of Skopje." Is this the subject of this document that we see in front of us?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the subject of this document: "Recruitment of 20 military conscripts in the sector of internal affairs of the city of Skopje."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at the second page, and you can see the number, 1D9769. The last paragraph there says the following: "The remaining conscripts, whose files have been selected but who do not meet the prescribed criteria for recruitment into reserve force of the SVR Skopje, are handed over to you for their potential deployment to other defence structures." When you spoke that the defence preparation unit could actually remove those who do not meet the requirements and transfer them to the Ministry of Defence, is this the situation that we read about in this document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kindly look now at the document in tab 40B.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1214.2. That is 1D9770, and the English page is 1D0044.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have, again, a document of the competent body within the sector of internal affairs for the city of Skopje sent to the Ministry of Defence. Tell me, before I ask you a question in relation to the document, tell me, please, where are the records maintained of all military conscripts in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The records are held in the regional units of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, this body of internal affairs would address the competent body that maintains the records of all conscripts. Is that understanding of mine correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Subject of this document is: "Report on reserve military conscripts stricken from the VOS of the SVR of Skopje city." The first paragraph says: "We hereby inform you that on the grounds that they do not meet the criteria envisaged for serving in the police reserve, the following reserve conscripts have been stricken from the records of the reserve police of the SVR Skopje," and then their names are indicated. Does this document also correspond to your knowledge and the practice, that if someone from within the reserve forces do not meet the requirements, they can only be sent back to the main records of the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, because I do not have much practice in this area, I know that this is the manner in which military conscripts are stricken off from the register.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And which is the body that issues such decision, which is the body that strikes of these persons' names and informs the body of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are sectors for internal affairs and the sections for defence preparations which work therein.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, could the minister strike off the name of a reserve force, or could they order someone to remove someone's name from the list of the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, not. That is an established procedure that is carried out by a specific organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, throughout the day today, we've been discussing employees of the Ministry of Interior and the conditions of their employment and work. Now, tell me, please, since you have worked in the ministry for many years, in all that time, were there any efforts made to improve the structure of those employed in the ministry, especially the ethnic structure within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Even then, I believe even earlier than this time, activities started to improve the representation of the ethnic minorities in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at tab 58 in the second binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's Exhibit 1D119; 1D4274 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report dated the 24th of April, 2001, and the subject is: "Negotiations with respect to the training of the newly recruited policemen in cooperation with the US Embassy in the Republic of Macedonia." Now, in view of the fact that you worked in the area of labour relations, do you know when efforts were started to change the ethnic structure and did this evolve throughout? Were there any problems along the way; and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere in the year 2000, the procedure for recruitment of new police officers in the Ministry of Interior commenced. Before that, the recruitment of police officers went through the recruiting graduates from the secondary police school, but the last group finished their education in 1999. So, in the next year, in the year 2000, activities started to recruit police officers through a public ad. I was then head of the personnel department. I know that during certain time, because of the ongoing activities, the procedure was interrupted and it continued sometime in September 2001, when we published the first ad for recruitment of police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The critical situation in Macedonia, did it have an effect on whereby it slowed down the process that had been initiated?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That was the main reason why was the process delayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've just said that, at the time, you were head of the personnel department up until the time that you became head of the legal and personnel affairs sector. So, in view of that, let's look at the following documents between tabs 59 and 65. Look through those and tell me whether you are familiar with those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, for the record, these are Exhibits 1D120, 1D121, 1D122, 1D123, 1D124.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with these documents; and if so, what do they refer to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. These are documents produced in the sector that I am the head of then and now, in the sector for personnel affairs; and they concern public ad for recruitment of 100 police officers in the Ministry of Interior published in several media outlets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, look at tab 64, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a 65 ter document, 1D1207; beginning with page 1D9683 in Macedonian and 1D0031 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'm familiar with this document. I know that during that time such brochures were produced, small brochures that were given to the police officers. I myself have such document in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when this particular document was printed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say when precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many copies of it was printed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the circulation was rather large, 1.000, 2.000. I really can't say precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We've already spoken about the fact that the director cannot be taken to task in disciplinary proceedings, and that the only thing that is possible is that the minister can propose that he be relieved of his duties. The proposal goes to the government who appointed him. Do you remember us discussing that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, can disciplinary measures be taken against the minister himself?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, not. The minister is an official elected by the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is he an employee of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is the -- does the collective agreement apply to the minister?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, on my count, you've asked these questions at least six times now, always getting the same answer. I think we might move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't counting, but probably I did repeat them quite a number of times. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are there separate laws governing the rights and duties of ministers and other officials who are elected and appointed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are such special laws, governing the matters of their salary, allowances, and other employment-related rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when we speak of disciplinary procedure, you said that disciplinary measures and proceedings can be taken against employees of the Ministry of Interior. Can you tell me who is authorised to set into motion a disciplinary measure or proceedings against an employee?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A proposal to initiate a disciplinary procedure could be filed by --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to move the binder away from the microphone and the witness to repeat the answer because we couldn't hear it because of the noise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do apologise. The Defence counsel seems to be under attack and criticism. It is obvious that Defence counsel is a little tired, so I apologise to the Trial Chamber and to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, could you answer that question, and the question was: Who is authorised to initiate disciplinary proceedings and what regulates that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the initiative, or are you referring to the commencement of a disciplinary procedure?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell us, first, since we saw some provisions on the rules an organisation of work, who can initiate disciplinary proceedings against an employee.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any superior officer could initiate a disciplinary procedure against an employee from within his subordination, while the proposal could be filed by the director of the bureaus for public security and for public safety and for sate security and the officers who are authorised by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you now, Ms. Dorevska, to take a look at a document we have already seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is tab 46, Exhibit P382.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I don't think it is here. I don't think it is in this binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is in binder 3; Tab 76, in binder 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask to you take a look at Article 143.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 143 is on page 27 of the English text; 6375, N002-6375.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, tell me, please, who tables a proposal? You already told us at whose initiative, but who tables a proposal that disciplinary proceedings be taken against an employee?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I answered this already, but I will repeat again. On the basis of Article 143, paragraph 5, it reads that the proposal is made by the under-secretary, the director of the directorate, and the officers authorised by the minister. Since the provisions of this collective agreement are a bit older, the proposals is made by the directors of the bureau and of the directorate and the officers that the minister authorises for this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, is the minister authorised himself to file a proposal for disciplinary proceedings to be taken?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The minister is not authorised to make a proposal to start a disciplinary procedure, and you can see it very clearly from this provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What authorisation of the minister is stipulated here?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this provision, the minister is obliged to authorise workers who can file a proposal for disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, why is it that the minister can't be the initiator of the disciplinary proceedings, why not?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the minister adopts the decision for a disciplinary measure; and, therefore, he cannot, at the same time, submit this proposal. This would mean that two matters would focus or would be placed in the person of one individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who conducts the proceedings to establish disciplinary responsibility and accountability of workers?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a special commission for dismissal which is established by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- well, we've said, as I understand it, the minister decides to set up a commission. He makes that decision. Secondly, he establishes who, in addition to these individuals, have the right to table the proposal. What else can a minister do with within these steps towards disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is obliged to pass the decision for a disciplinary measure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when does he do that? When does he pass that decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, when the dismissal commission, on the basis of the previous initiative and proposal, will finish the procedure foreseen for that issue and will propose to the minister a certain measure against a specific individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While the commission is conducting the proceedings, does the minister enjoy any rights, does very any rights in interfering in the proceedings or taking part in the proceedings at all?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The minister cannot take part in the proceeding and cannot at all interfere in the work of the commission. The commission is -- is independent in its proceedings on disciplinary matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you said that the minister makes the decisions. What decision, after the procedure has been put in place and conducted, what decision can the minister take?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the proposal of the commission, the minister can adopt a decision on dismissal, termination of employment; and at the proposal of the commission, this termination of employment can be replaced with a fee, a fine, for a period of one to six months.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This decision by the minister, with respect to disciplinary responsibility and accountability, is it final?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This decision is it not final, because the employee can always appeal to the second instance commission at the government which decides in areas related to labour issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What can that second instance commission actually do?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This commission can take into account the appeal of the employee, can change the decision of the minister; and in this case, this decision of the second instance commission is obligatory for the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you to take up the second binder and to look at tab 72, the document there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 65 ter 1D1266, and it on page 1D0135.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I have the third binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After tab 72, it is 1D0135; and in English, it's 1D0161.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the preamble of this act, we can see that in referring to the legal basis, legal grounds, the commission for the second instance commission decides on an appeal that has been lodged. Is that the commission that you have just testified about, this second instance commission, which deals with appeals to the ministerial decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the second instance commission in the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we can see, this decision passed a decision; and below, it says that the appeal is granted, as founded. Does that confirm what you said, that the second instance commission can uphold the minister's decision or reject it on appeal?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly so. This is one manner in which way the commission can reach a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the procedure according to which the second instance commission works, or the government commission?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This commission works on the basis of the provisions of the Law on Government which regulates the work of the commissions, but also there is also a Book of Rules about its work which establishes the manner and the procedures for the work of this commission and the decisions that it can adopt.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now look at tab 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter exhibit [as interpreted] 1D1267. 0137 is the page number in Macedonian, and 1D0163 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, these rules of procedure, are they the rules according to which the government commission works, that you've just talked about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a rule of procedure for the work of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When an employee is in transgression of a duty, what is the deadline within which proceedings can be taken against a particular employee, or are there any deadlines? Is there any statute of limitations after which time disciplinary measures can not be taken?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is such a deadline established with the collective agreement. This is a period of three months from the day of learning of the violation. This is objective [as interpreted]. Six months, an objective, once this is repeated once, these deadlines have been surpassed. The disciplinary procedure cannot be repeated because of the existence of a statute of limitations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, Ms. Dorevska, let us take a look at some documents found in binder 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 50/1 -- no, I apologise. Page 58, line 1, or rather, on 58, line 1, something was erroneously recorded, because she was speaking about a "subjective" deadline of three months, and an objective deadline of six months.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, Witness?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at tab 105, which is a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of which is 1D1271. And it is page 1D0185; and in the English, it is 0187.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, what does this document represent?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision by which, after a procedure for an individual, employment is terminated without a period for termination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who passes this decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision is reached by the minister at the proposal of the commission who led the proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at tab 106 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 65 ter 1D1272. Page 1D0191 in Macedonian, and 1D0192 in the English. Yes, 0190, Macedonian; and 0192, English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, what does this document represent, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an objection of an employee against a decision of the Ministry of Internal Affairs by which, I presume, the employee has been issued a decision for termination of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at tab 107, which is 65 ter 1D1273.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And on page 1D0194 of the Macedonian, and 1D0196 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, can you tell me, please, what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a case when an employee objects before the second instance commission of the government, then this proceeding is carried out in a way that this objection is submitted through the body which adopted the decision. In this case, the objection comes to the sector which I head at the moment, and then this sector as a specialised service prepares an opinion in regards to this objection, which is submitted to the second instance commission at the government. It can happen that the objection is submitted directly to the commission at the government. However, this will be returned back to the Ministry of Interior, so as it can receive it from the ministry, that is to say, can receive an opinion whether this objection is grounded or not grounded, which does not bind the commission in any way. Of course, this can only be in the interest of making this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question, Ms. Dorevska, which relates to tab 108, 65 ter 1D1274.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0198 is the page in Macedonian, and 0200 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision of the second instance commission at the government which has decided that the objection is rejected as ungrounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that completes my examination of the witness. During the break, I will provide a list of exhibits -- or rather, documents which I put to the witness, which are not included in the list of exhibits that the Prosecutor has, in order to facilitate their work and rather to facilitate the work of the Trial Chamber in makes its decisions [as interpreted]. Yes. I have been told that there's a problem with the interpretation. I said that these documents are still not exhibits, but they are on the list of our documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have the break now and resume at 1.00. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as I said, I have submitted the list of documents that we wished to tender to my learned colleague, so I will first seek to tender the documents that the Prosecution does not object to. So I seek to tender the following documents: 65 ter 1D1200, which was in tab 9 and is the rule book on the work of the sector for intelligence and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender in evidence 65 ter document 1216, which was in tab 70. That is the decision of the constitutional court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We seek to tender into evidence the 65 ter document 1D1217. That was in tab 71, which is the second decision of -- or another decision of the constitutional court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D299.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We seek to tender into evidence 65 ter 1D1218 [as interpreted], which is in tab 45. That is the decision about the remuneration on -- for the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We seek to tender into evidence 65 ter 1D1209 and 1D1210, in tabs 46 and 47 respectively, which are again related to remuneration for the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Together they will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D1209 will become Exhibit 1D301, and 65 ter 1D1210 will become Exhibit 1D302.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1D1207 which is in tab 64, and they are rules -- I apologise. 1D1207, that is the rules of the Ministry of Interior related to the security bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D303, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender into evidence 65 ter 1D1271, which is in tab 105. That is a decision about the disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender into evidence 65 ter 1D1272 in tab 106, and that is an appeal against a minister's decision on termination of employment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender into evidence 65 ter 1D1273 in tab 107, which is a response from the ministry to the appeal that was lodged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor's office objected to the following documents that the Defence wishes to tender. These are 65 ter 1D1214.1. That was in tab 42 [as interpreted], and it pertains to the conditions or the procedure through which the reservists are removed from the forces of the Ministry of Interior and transferred to the Ministry of Defence. At the same time, 65 ter 1214.2. That was in tab 40B. That, again, speaks about striking out names of reservists who do not meet the requirements from the list and their transfer again to the Ministry of Defence. The Defence proposes that these documents are received as relevant documents because, on the one hand, they are authentic; on the other hand, they are relevant since they show in which was the only way that the ministry could react, versus the reserve forces when they do not meet the necessary requirements or prerequisites for a person to be a member of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 62/14, "40A," letter A, instead of "42."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, on those two proposed exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're objecting because those two proposed exhibits arise from a later time-period. 65 ter 1D1214.1 at tab 40A is dated 8 April 2004, and 65 ter 1D1214.2 at tab 40B is dated 16 April 2004; and so, therefore, the Prosecution fails to see the relevance of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will not be received. Now does that complete your list of exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two more that the Prosecutor's office objected to: 65 ter 1D1266 in tab 72 and 65 ter 1D1267 in tab 73. Decision of the second instance committee which show in which way the second instance committee decided upon appeals of employees against minister's decision, and the second document speaks about the rules of procedure of the committee used by the committee when making such decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to 65 ter 1D1266, once again it is a decision that falls outside of the relevant time-period. It was delivered on the 22nd of August 2007, and the preamble of the decision refers to laws and regulations that are respectively in 2003, 2005, 2007. So, in my submission, again that would be irrelevant to the proceedings. With respect 65 ter 1267, which is the rules of procedure, once against it appears that these rules were adopted on the 2nd of April 2003. So their relevance is -- well, they're irrelevant in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do believe that the witness answered some of the objections. Could you allow me that, before you make your decision, I ask one additional question of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I really don't think it would help, Ms. Residovic. My own objection is we have oral evidence that there was a second instance committee established at the government level to which appeals could be taken. Though independent of the minister, they made decisions against decisions of the minister. What more do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I'm satisfied with your statement, and I do not insist to submit these documents as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will not be received. Thank you. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Dorevska. Just if I can introduce myself.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: My name is Antoinette Issa and I work for the Prosecutor's office and I'm here on their behalf, and I would just like to ask you a few questions. First of all, I've noted, in your examination-in-chief, you've indicated that you've had a very long career with the ministry and you kind of went over your work rather quickly. So I'd like just to highlight a few things, if I may. I understand that, on 10 April 2001, you had been assigned to the post of the head officer of personnel department for the sector of legal and personnel matters by then Minister Dosta Dimovska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then, on the 1st of October in 2001, you were reassigned to another place of duty as head officer to the personnel department, again in the sector for legal and personnel matters, and you were given an increase in your salary at that point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not sure that I understood your question well. I believe you mentioned the same workplace?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there an increase in your salary in October 2001 and a reassignment at that point?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In October 2001, I received a contract for head of legal and personnel affairs; and, yes, I received a raise in my salary.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that was done at the time that Minister Boskoski was then in office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then two months later, in January of 2002, you were promoted to assistant to the minister in the sector for legal and personnel matters. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. This was the identical workplace. I mentioned this during my testimony. Previously, I was head of the same sector because the name of the workplace, the title of that workplace was such, but this was a temporary decision. At the beginning of 2002 I was assigned assistant to the minister because the name of the -- the title of the workplace had changed; otherwise, it is the same workplace in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And then you continued in this post; and as I understand it, in September 2002, which was six months later, you received an increase in salary or cash bonus, once again. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. In October 2001, when I received the first decision as the head officers and the later decision for the same work post with the title assistant minister, I did not -- I did not receive an ensuing decision. I'm still at the same work post.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, you misunderstood me. What I asked what was whether you received an increase in your salary or a cash bonus, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean remuneration, yes, a bonus, yes; but this is not a raise there salary. My salary was the same established with the decision which served to my assignment, but a bonus or any other type of reward is an altogether different matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned, Ms. Dorevska, that your tasks at the ministry in 2001, and I guess to the present day, entail drafting laws and regulations and to deal with matters of human remain resources and management and things of that nature. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you also work -- you said today, I believe, that you deal with personnel matters as well.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still work on personnel issues; but, at this moment, there is a different organisation to it, and it is somewhat different than the period in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But just staying with the period in question, which is in 2001/2002, those were essentially your tasks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, prior to your work at the Ministry of Interior, you had not worked as a police officer, had you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not worked. I said I had a voluntary apprenticeship at the commercial court prior to my employment at the minister. Even now, I'm not a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you also mentioned, I believe in your direct testimony, that you never went out and executed a search warrant or had anything to do with operative tasks. So I take it you've never worked on investigations of -- of crimes, have you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have never worked on these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you have never been out in the field assisting or you were never present at a police operation, have you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I take it you never accompanied Minister Boskoski at the time in the field.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that also Minister Boskoski was never on the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But that's something that you -- how do you know that? What makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a presumption. I'm not sure about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So that's just your belief. Now, clearly, you've done well for yourself, Ms. Dorevska, because you have been promoted several times, and I take it that you take your work very seriously and that you're conscientious at what you do. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And as assistant to the minister at the time, in 2001, did you have supervisory duties?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. What do you mean by "supervisory duties."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you said you were the head of sector for legal affairs and personnel. So presumably you had people that were working for in that sector. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I had over 30 people in the sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did those people that you supervise report to you regarding the tasks that they carried out?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Above all, they reported to their direct superiors because there were two sections which part of my sector, but also to me as head officer of the sector through their section heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that you had people working for you that had immediate superiors, but you were the -- the head of the entire sector and so you received reports up that chain to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I take it, Ms. Dorevska, that these reports concerned information regarding the work of your particular sector and the ongoing tasks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I take it, as -- as the superior and as the head of the sector, that you relied upon these reports in order to help you make decisions regarding the work of the sector. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And sometimes, based on the information that you received, did you delegate some tasks to your subordinates or to people in the sector?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This is one of the basic principle of work to delegate certain competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's part of your rule, as a supervisor or the head of the sector at the time, that to know when to delegate certain tasks and other times to carry out those tasks yourself. That would be a basic principle. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And as assistant to the minister in -- for that sector, you said that you were subordinate to the minister or you were directly linked to the minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. This is a sector which functionally is related to the work of the minister. It is directly connected to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So, presumably, you reported to the minister about your tasks and activities as well. Is that -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the collegium which were held, I always gave reports about the work of my sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you give reports to the minister outside of the collegium as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reports, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you -- did you give information outside of the -- of the collegium as well; if not reports, did you provide him with information?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If the minister so requested for a certain matter, I was -- I'm duty-bound to provide information to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if there was a matter that you felt was of importance that should come to his attention as the minister, wouldn't you also provide him with that information?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I would provide that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Because that would, of course, permit him to make decisions as the minister on the basis of the information that you provide, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did sometimes the minister give you instructions in relation to certain activities or tasks that he wished -- he wanted to have carried out?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never gave me instructions. They were always conversations where certain matters were decided, matters which sector should undertake as its task.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, suppose the minister had said to you that he wanted a particular matter in your sector to be carried out in a -- in a specific way, would you follow that request?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above all, I would point out to him what can be done in that regard, and this did happen. The request of the minister is always supported with my professional indications; and if conditions are met, then, of course, the work will be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So what you're telling us, then, is that you would give him your views and your opinion on how you think a particular matter should be carried out; and, in the end, he may decide that should be carried out in a particular way. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in 2001, Ms. Dorevska, at that time, there was an ongoing conflict, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And there was a crisis in 2001 that put great pressure on the work of the ministry, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In fact, you've just explained earlier today that certain public announcements for training of employees were not made during that period, because of the great pressure and stress in -- because of the crisis, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Activities were halted regarding the publishing public announcements for hiring police officers, not for training.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But they were halted because of the -- of the pressure, of the complex security situation as a result of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, in fact, the security situation was so serious at the time that reservists had to be called up to assist the regular Macedonian forces in 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a concrete answer to this question, because I don't know how the decision was passed for the call-up of reserve forces. But I can presume, due to the serious nature of the situation, that it was essential to increase the number of police officers or rather, to call up the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And just moving, then, on to another topic. You've explained yesterday to us, Ms. Dorevska, that the directors or the director of the bureau of public safety, or public security, and the other director of counter-intelligence and security, are appointed by the government on proposal of the minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, equally, you've said that the minister can issue a proposal to the government to have the director removed, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can submit a proposal for his dismissal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the director is responsible for the work of the body that he manages to the minister, as well as to the government. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the law that you referred to yesterday makes it is clear that the director is accountable or answerable to the minister.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is answerable to the minister, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, in fact, what I believe you said in your testimony is that the director is primarily accountable to the minister because he is part of ministry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So does the director report to the minister about his tasks and the work of the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if the director is responsible for his work to the minister, doesn't that also mean that the minister can check the quality of his work?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how he would check that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't the director, if, say, the director reported to the minister about some task that he undertook and the minister wasn't very happy with the way in which the director carried out that task, can the minister, for example, tell him to revise the task or change it somehow?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe to an extent, yes, as a result of some collegium within which decisions are made of strategic importance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But if the -- assuming, then, if the director's work was not of good quality or the minister was not happy with the way in which the director was carrying out his tasks in general, then what you've told us is that the minister can propose to have the director dismissed to the government. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. And to elaborate it, before the government presenting facts why he is not satisfied with the work of the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And, presumably, the director knows that he is in the position of director because he was given that post after a proposal was made by the minister to make him director. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is probably right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you would presume that if that's how things worked and that's how the director got his post, he would know that the -- he received the post as a result of the proposal made by the minister. Isn't that just -- isn't that logical?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a procedure for appointing the director, and every director is appointed following that same procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So the director knows, practically speaking, that it would be foolish to do anything that contravened the minister's wishes, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, the wishes of the minister are irrelevant for the performance of the duties in the area of public safety and state security. These are precisely defined obligations that they have the duty to follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that that's what you said the way things work. But, practically speaking, Ms. Dorevska, you've told us that the director reports to the minister regarding his tasks, and you've told us that the minister has some say in the quality or -- on the quality of the work of the director. Don't you think that the director might be influenced by a concern that he didn't wish to contravene the minister's wishes?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think like that at all, because the ministry, and I will repeat it again, does not work according to the wishes of the minister. It works pursuant to the legislation and the constitution of the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What if the director was at a collegium with the minister and the minister suggested or asked the director to carry out a specific task that is within his competence and the director didn't do it properly or didn't do it according the wishes of the minister, couldn't the minister at that stage propose to remove the director?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever the minister is not satisfied with the work of the director, the minister could always submit a proposal, but that proposal must always be corroborated by other facts. One single situation where the minister is not satisfied with the activity as it was carried out could not be sufficient grounds for removal of the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But let's just say that it's not one single activity. Let's just say it's a number of activities that the director simply was not carrying out the tasks in the way that the minister would have liked to see.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the assessment of the minister. If the minister assesses that the director performed the duties unconsciously or undiligently, I would repeat again, the minister can submit a proposal and inform the government. The government is the body appointing and dismissing the director, and the government will decide whether the work of the director was proper, satisfactory, or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if the director makes a specific proposal to the minister, can the minister disagree with the proposal that the director has made.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could disagree, depending on what is the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned that in 2001, the director of bureau for public security was Goran Mitevski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I believe that, without going to the exhibit, you were shown an exhibit, 1D105, where we saw that Goran Mitevski was appointed, on 15 May 2001, as director of public security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that was two days after Ljube Boskoski was appointed as minister. He was appointed on 13 May, 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it didn't take very long for Goran Mitevski to be appointed, did it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever a new minister comes to the office, the team around the minister arrives simultaneously. That is a rule in the ministry. And in all other ministries, the minister, deputy ministers, state secretary, and the directors are political figures that are the makeup of the team during given periods. I don't see anything illogical in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the minister can decide on the team that he wishes to have around him, including the director of public security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one can say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In November 2002, when Ljube Boskoski left the office of the minister, Goran Mitevski also left the ministry altogether. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And isn't that true, Ms. Dorevska, that, historically, people sometimes, when a new minister entered office, he may transfer people and shift people around, some people get demoted, and others leave. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happens, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that happens because of the relationships of trust that develop between people and the different political allegiances. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't make such assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, in November 2002, when Ljube Boskoski left, his former advisor, Zoran Krstevski, left as well, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't remember the precise time when Mr. Krstevski left. I know that he left the office of his own will.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, he left shortly after Ljube Boskoski left, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And Sofija Galeva, who was the state advisor within the cabinet of the ministry, she also left the ministry as well, around that time, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. She did not leave the ministry. She was assigned to a different post.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. She was assigned to a different post around the time right after Ljube Boskoski left.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were many shifts after Mr. Boskoski left and after the power changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you Ms. Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am aware of the time, and I was to move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now. We resume on Monday at 2.15. I'm afraid we must ask you to come back on Monday, Ms. Dorevska. Thank you very much. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of February, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
